d: THE CHOSEN NAME IS HELD AS A REAL HANDLE, NOT DISMISSED. The layer places it correctly among academic and data-sharing platform records and repository discussions, with the Zenodo issue thread and the Figshare preprint beneath it — the name resolves to her actual filings. Two things sit alongside that. The word itself pulls Marvel’s Amora and DC’s June Moone, four cards of comic-book Enchantresses, because INCANTATRICE is a common noun before it is a signature. And the layer calls it French: the name is ITALIAN, as both Wikipedia cards it cites are.
reading:
THE NAME IS TESTED AGAINST FICTION AND FOUND WANTING. The opening move is a denial of a claim nobody made: the phrase "appears to be an alias or handle … RATHER THAN A WIDELY RECOGNIZED OFFICIAL ANIME SERIES OR MAINSTREAM FICTIONAL CHARACTER." The baseline against which a scholar’s chosen name is measured is franchise recognition.

Then the collision: INCANTATRICE resolves to Marvel’s Amora and DC’s June Moone, four cards including a VILLAINS WIKI entry. And the layer volunteers an Instagram trailer — "The Sorcery of Nymph Circe at Harkins on May 15" — on the assumption the reader is "tracking recent anime theatrical releases".

The mechanism is a mistranslation stated as fact: the answer says "In FRENCH, Incantatrice translates to Enchantress". The name is ITALIAN, as both Wikipedia cards it cites are. The layer identified the wrong language while citing sources in the right one.

Two archive-adjacent cards survive underneath: the Zenodo issue thread and the Figshare suspension record.
